title: Feasibility note: splitting a model across bases
goal: A design note says whether and how NERV could run one model across two bases with llama.cpp RPC
acceptance: docs/design/model-splitting.md names the target model, runtime, routing and enrolment join, security boundary and an expected throughput range with its source
It states when splitting is not worth it (the model fits one base)

It compares the split with single-base alternatives: AirLLM (layer-by-layer from disk, roughly 7-10 s per token for a 40 GB model on a 5-6 GB/s SSD) and llama.cpp memory-mapped offload, by tokens per second, setup and fit for NERV's Node/Ollama stack
The throughput estimate (about 1.5-3 tok/s for a ~40 GB model split Mac + mini PC, bound by memory bandwidth, not the network) is checked against the mini PC's actual specs
privacy: No real host names, addresses or credentials in Git.
escalation: Installing runtimes or running models on a base waits for the owner

effort.basis: Estimated 2026-11-22: reading llama.cpp RPC docs and NERV's routing, one note. Not a measurement.
